record.question:
Write the precis of the following passage, giving it a suitable title:                         (14)
             The FIFA World Cup is the globe’s most prestigious football tournament, held every four
   years by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA). Uniting billions of fans and
   national teams, this monumental event transcends sports, serving as a powerful engine for global
   unity, cultural exchange, and international economic growth.
             Often referred to as the “beautiful Game,” football has a universal appeal that requires
   nothing more than a ball and an open space. The World Cup serves as the pinnacle of this sport,
   elevating the passion of local communities onto the international stage. Every four years, it captures
   the attention of a massive global audience, making it the most-watched sporting event on the planet.
   For participating nations, the tournament is a profound source of national pride, where everyday life
   pauses as communities gather to cheer for their country’s color.
            The tournament was first established in 1930 under the vision of then-FIFA President Jules
   Rimet. Since its inaugural competition in Uruguay, the event has grown exponentially in scale and
   competitive intensity. Over the decades, legendary teams and iconic players—such as Pelé, Diego
   Maradona, and Lionel Messi—have etched their names into sports history, creating enduring legacies.
   The event has also adapted to modern demands, integrating advanced technology like Video Assistant
   Referee (VAR) systems to ensure fairness and accuracy in high-stakes matches.
             Beyond the thrill of the matches, the World Cup carries profound socio-economic and
   cultural significance. It acts as a massive cultural melting pot, allowing diverse sets of fans from
   various backgrounds to share traditions, celebrate together, and foster mutual understanding. For the
   host nation, the World Cup is a massive undertaking that brings in billions of dollars through tourism,
   sponsorships, and media rights, while driving infrastructure development like modern stadiums and
   transport networks.
             The FIFA World Cup is more than just a month-long sporting competition; it is a global
   phenomenon that brings humanity together in a shared passion. Despite political and logistical
   challenges, its ability to unite people across borders, languages, and cultures remains unparalleled.
   The tournament leaves a lasting legacy by inspiring generations of young players, cementing national
   identities, and celebrating the sheer joy of the beautiful game.

record.passage:
As the 23rd conference of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change in Bonn shifts
into high gear, developing countries including India are focussing on the imperatives of ensuring adequate
financing for mitigation and adaptation. They are moving ahead with specific instruments for loss and
damage they suffer due to destructive climate-linked events. India’s progress in reducing the intensity
of its greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP by 20-25% from 2005 levels by 2020, based on the
commitment made in Copenhagen in 2009, has been positive. Early studies also suggest that it is on
track to achieve the national pledge under the 2015 Paris Agreement for a 33-35% cut in emissions
intensity per unit of growth from the same base year by 2030, and thus heed the 2°C warming goal.
Since this performance is predicated on a growth rate of just over 7%, and the parallel target for 40%
share of renewable energy by that year, the national road map is clear. What is not, however, is the
impact of extreme weather events such as droughts and floods that would have a bearing on economic
growth. It is in this context that the rich countries must give up their rigid approach towards the
demands of low and middle income countries, and come to an early resolution on the question of
financing of mitigation, adaptation and compensation. Of course, India could further raise its ambition
in the use of green technologies and emissions cuts, which would give it the mantle of global climate
leadership.

The climate question presents a leapfrog era for India’s development paradigm. Already, the
country has chalked out an ambitious policy on renewable energy, hoping to generate 175 gigawatts
of power from green sources by 2022. This has to be resolutely pursued, breaking down the barriers
to wider adoption of rooftop solar energy at every level and implementing net metering systems for all
categories of consumers. At the Bonn conference, a new Transport Decarbonisation Alliance has
been declared. It is aimed at achieving a shift to sustainable fuels, getting cities to commit to eco-
friendly mobility and delivering more walkable communities, all of which will improve the quality of
urban life. This presents a good template for India, building on its existing plans to introduce electric
mobility through buses first, and cars by 2030. Such measures will have a beneficial effect not just on
transport choices, but on public health through pollution abatement.

To understand the elements of the policy and regulatory environment, we first identify the
characteristics of 5G, Unlike earlier generations that provided for ever higher speeds and more
bandwidth, 5G also promises ultra-reliable, very fast speeds and high bandwidth mobile connectivity
and supports massive interconnected devices spread across wide areas. 5G provides peak speeds of
20 times, compared with 4G, such as that required in virtual reality applications, It is also designed to
provide latency at 10 times lower than 4G, Low latency is required in applications dealing with critical
emergency health care, autonomous vehicles or disaster management. Since 5G roll-outs are likely
even before 4G is extensively deployed, the adopted road map for 5G should ensure that the existing
and near-future investments in 4G can be leveraged. One suggested approach has been that since
operators are likely to deploy 5G in bands that they are currently using for 4G, policy should facilitate
this by making spectrum usage an agnostic service. The role of wired infrastructure, especially fibre

optic cables, is critical and complementary to growth of wireless. This is because very large capacities
are required in the backhaul to cater to applications enabled through 5G This would entail accelerating
the Bharat Net Programme for deploying fibre optic cables to gram panchayats and increasing the
involvement of the private sector to exploit complementarities and efficiencies of the private sector.

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
(a) What has been the primary function of social media in its early days, according to the passage? (1)
(b) How has social media evolved in the past decade? (1)
(c) Which platforms are mentioned in the passage as popular social media sites? (1)
(d) What are some of the positive impacts of social media mentioned in the passage? (1)
(e) In what way does social media influence public opinion during times of crisis? (1)
(f) How has social media affected face-to-face communication? (2)
(g) What is the impact of constant notifications on individuals, as mentioned in the passage? (2)
(h) According to the passage, why is social media described as a “double-edged sword”? (2)
(i) What advice does the passage offer regarding social media usage? (2)
(j) Mention any three negative consequences of social media highlighted in the passage? (3)
(k) Find words from the passage similar in meaning to: (i) Sense (ii) Distinction. (1+1=2)
(l) Find words from the passage opposite in meaning to: (i) Diminish (ii) Refrain. (1+1=2)

record.passage:
The rise of social media over the past decade has dramatically changed the way people
communicate, share information, and perceive the world. What began as a tool for social interaction
has now evolved into a powerful platform that influences politics, business, and culture. Platforms
like Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram allow users to connect with friends and family, but they also
enable individuals to express their opinions to a global audience. However, the widespread use of
social media has led to both positive and negative consequences. On the one hand, it has democratized
communication, giving voice to people from all walks of life. On the other hand, it has created an
environment where misinformation spreads easily, and individuals often find themselves trapped in
echo chambers that reinforce their own beliefs. As a result, the impact of social media on society is a
topic of ongoing debate.

While social media has made it easier to stay connected, it has also led to a decline in face-to-
face interactions. People increasingly rely on online communication, which can sometimes lack the
nuance and depth of in-person conversations. Moreover, the constant stream of information and
notifications can lead to a sense of overload and stress, making it difficult for individuals to disconnect
from the digital world. Despite these challenges, social media continues to play a central role in
shaping public opinion, especially during times of crisis, such as elections or global pandemics.

In conclusion, social media is a double-edged sword: it offers both immense opportunities and
significant challenges. As users, it is essential to navigate this space thoughtfully, ensuring that we use
these platforms responsibly while remaining aware of their potential drawbacks.
